text: [precision] Always re-verify each finding against the PR's current head commit before reporting, and drop any finding anchored to lines that a later commit in the same PR rewrote or deleted.

[precision] Treat deliberate diffs to defaults, constants, settings schemas, and cancellation/steering flags as the point of the PR — check the PR description and 'Out of scope' notes first, only flag when the change contradicts the PR's own stated intent or tests, and assume a code-vs-comment mismatch means the comment is stale, not the code.

[precision] Never flag Effect API usage from memory: verify against the repo's pinned effect@4.0.0-beta typings and patches/, since in v4 Equal.equals is deep-structural on plain objects, Predicate.isObject excludes arrays, Option.makeOrder exists, Command exit codes are never null, runFold/mapAccum accept LazyArg initial values, and POSIX spawns default to detached.

[precision] In Effect/React code, don't report a multi-step failure chain (fiber leak, stale flag, stream consumed twice) unless you can trace every branch condition end-to-end and name a concrete executable path, because such chains usually die on mutually-exclusive conditionals.

[precision] Check the pinned runtime and toolchain (Electron 41/Node 22 where networkInterfaces family is the string 'IPv4', Linux-capable titlebar APIs like setTitleBarOverlay, CI installs frozen by default, platform-specific pnpm package dirs, web clients often in non-secure contexts) before flagging platform-availability, lockfile, or compatibility issues.

[precision] Before flagging missing validation, dedup, or cleanup at a call site, search the surrounding function and other layers (upstream normalizers, server-guaranteed ordering such as DFS pre-order process lists, client stores that dedupe subscriptions) because cross-file invariants are the norm in this repo.

[precision] Before flagging a possible undefined or mismatched value, check the declared TypeScript/Electron/contract types — if the failing scenario can't typecheck (e.g., a required string field or a union that excludes the value), don't report it, and remember optional chaining short-circuits whole access chains.

[precision] Before calling a refactor a regression, diff the actual behavior against origin/main and only flag deltas the PR itself introduced — never attribute pre-existing base-branch behavior to the diff.

[precision] For any 'X is inverted/backwards' claim about comparators, boolean flags, viewport/drag directions, or CSS overrides, verify against the authoritative definition (vendored headers, the comparator's actual contract, rendered behavior) before flagging, because these directional claims are wrong as often as the code.

[precision] Confirm the actual domain of the input (what providers/APIs really emit and what consumers really read) before flagging an edge case, and don't report failures that require data shapes or races the current system cannot produce or whose effect no consumer observes.

[precision] Don't file style or UX preferences (icon-component dedup, where error text surfaces, fallback label choices) as findings — maintainers deliberately keep duplicated SVG icon components and accept detail being one click away, so only report measurable functional defects.

[recall] For every Effect error-channel operator (orDie, Effect.option, orElseSucceed, catchTag, bare runPromise) in apps/server and apps/desktop, ask which specific error it should absorb: broad absorbers hide transient fs/network failures as empty data, orDie turns recoverable decode failures into crashes, and bare Effect.runPromise needs a .catch or it takes down the ws server.

[recall] Any regex or split()-based parser of tool output or identifiers (SSH/git/CLI stderr, model keys, keybindings, hosts, registry paths) must be checked against IPv6 colons, extra delimiters, quotes, empty segments, localized OS messages, and detached-HEAD-style variants — hotspots are packages/ssh, apps/desktop/src/sshEnvironment.ts, apps/server/src/cli/invocation.ts, and packages/shared/keybindings.ts.

[recall] Every await or callback that writes into shared state (store, read model, draft, Ref) must re-validate the active thread/project/provider/environment id or a generation counter after resuming, since context-switch-during-await is the single most common real bug in ChatView.tsx, mobile thread screens, orchestration reactors, and client-runtime state.

[recall] For any path, process, or binary-detection change in apps/desktop/src/backend, apps/desktop/src/wsl, sshEnvironment.ts, or server CLI detection, explicitly trace the Windows and WSL branches: backslashes, drive letters, .exe suffixes, registry-quoted values, pnpm/bun cache layouts on Windows, and wsl.exe-present-but-no-distro states.

[recall] Whenever a .find/map lookup or function argument involves one of this repo's parallel id spaces (threadId, projectId, environmentId, sessionId, draft keys, instance ids), verify the id's type actually matches the collection's key, because ChatView.tsx alone has produced dozens of id swaps that branded strings don't catch once stringified.

[recall] In apps/mobile, review every Platform.OS, split-view, or native-chrome early return for what the skipped branch loses (search, headers, filters), and treat React Navigation setParams/deep-link handlers plus the Swift native modules (t3-review-diff, t3-composer-editor) as high-defect zones needing coordinate/offset re-derivation checks.

[recall] For any emitter, pubsub publish, or in-flight coalescing in provider adapters, ghostty IME handling, and mobile notification/share flows, check both directions: whether the same logical event can fire twice (needs an idempotency key) and whether a concurrent duplicate request drops its caller's callbacks instead of joining the in-flight one — and verify dedupe sets get pruned.

[recall] For every Deferred, gate, or promise a caller awaits, enumerate all exits (dispose, error, process-already-exited, cancellation) and confirm each one resolves or rejects it, specifically hunting check-then-register races on child 'exit' listeners in ssh/pty code and settlement conditions in orchestration-v2 adapters.

[recall] In apps/web/src/components (ChatView.tsx is the top hotspot), audit each effect/memo for omitted dependencies and each piece of pending/override/boolean-flag state for an explicit reset when the thread, file, or panel it belongs to changes.

[recall] In apps/server/src/resourceTelemetry and native/resource-monitor, any delta or cumulative-counter computation must handle process disappearance-and-return, PID reuse/exec, category reclassification, out-of-order sampledAtUnixMs, and counter reset after recovery.

[recall] Review every dispose/close/unmount for the full inventory it must undo — IPC channel handlers, signal 'abort' listeners, debounce timers, outbound queues, and in-flight async ops — and check that late completions and post-dispose calls no-op rather than throw or resurrect state (worst offenders: apps/desktop/src/sshEnvironment.ts, provider adapters, wsTransport).

[recall] Whenever a default is applied via ??, ||, Boolean coercion, or Number(), test the explicit falsy inputs (0, '', false, null) separately from undefined, because this codebase repeatedly clobbers deliberate user opt-outs and custom config with defaults, especially in settings normalization and CLI flag parsing.

[recall] Treat apps/web/src/terminal/ghostty/* as a specialist review zone: check IME composition state machines for double or dropped commits, event.key vs event.code semantics, UTF-16 code units vs bytes vs graphemes in buffer math, and which coordinate space (viewport row vs terminal buffer row) selection APIs return.

[recall] Wherever git/PR CLI output or search results pass through a byte or count cap (GitVcsDriverCore, pullRequest/*Cli.ts, WorkspaceSearchIndex), verify the truncated flag is computed from the raw capped stream, checked before JSON decoding, and propagated to every caller rather than hardcoded.

[recall] Every subscribe-then-snapshot (or snapshot-then-subscribe) pairing across the websocket read-model bridge needs an explicit ordering argument — attach and buffer the live stream first, then apply the snapshot, then replay — plus version checks so a stale snapshot or persisted cache can never overwrite newer streamed state.

[precision] Desktop mock-update tooling (--mock-updates in scripts/build-desktop-artifact.ts, T3CODE_DESKTOP_MOCK_UPDATES in apps/desktop/src/main.ts) is strictly opt-in dev tooling: GitHub publish config intentionally takes precedence over mock updates, and truthy env parsing is intended; don't flag config-precedence or lenient boolean parsing on these paths unless default no-flag behavior is affected.

[precision] Maintainers do not SHA-pin GitHub Actions (all workflows use mutable refs like actions/checkout@v6, expo actions @main per vendor docs); never raise action-pinning/supply-chain-hardening findings on this repo's workflows — workflow-behavior bugs remain valid.

[precision] OpenCode integration: `opencode models --verbose` and `opencode agent list` do not require a working directory (the SDK's directory param was only for HTTP-server session config), and empty CLI inventory intentionally maps to warning status (zero providers is itself the failure signal; the 5-minute refresh self-heals). Don't flag missing cwd on runOpenCodeCommand inventory calls or warning-vs-error taxonomy there.

[precision] In apps/server/src/cli/pair.ts, classifying HTTP 502/503/504 from the Tailscale Serve probe as unreachable (allowing reconfigure) is an explicit product decision so `t3 pair --tailscale` can repair stale Serve mappings; don't re-flag it as a guard bypass.

[precision] ChatComposer: an image paste/drop gesture synchronously clearing the previous thread-error banner is established intended UX; only flag thread-error clearing that happens after an await where in-flight errors get wiped.
